page: Google Cloud Platform c4-highmem-144 is a high-capacity server instance belonging to the c4 family, configured with 144 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 72 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 6985P-C processor. Operating at a base clock speed of 2.3 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, this instance features a substantial 504 MB L3 cache. It is equipped with 1116.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 7.75 GB per vCPU. The instance does not include local storage or integrated GPU hardware, meaning all storage requirements must be met via network-attached volumes.

Benchmark evaluations place this instance in the top tier for multi-core processing and memory throughput. It achieves a stress-ng multi-core CPU performance score of 156247.55 and a PassMark CPU score of 134960.09, reflecting its massive parallel processing capability. Memory bandwidth is exceptionally high, with read-only large block speeds reaching 533.18 GB/sec and write speeds at 205.98 GB/sec. The processor's advanced instruction support, including AVX-512 and Intel AMX (Advanced Matrix Extensions), drives top-tier results in cryptographic operations, database transactions, and LLM inference prompt processing. However, single-core performance remains in the average tier, as demonstrated by a stress-ng single-core score of 2299.89.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c4-highmem-144 offers high resource density for workloads requiring massive memory footprints alongside heavy multi-threaded compute, avoiding the overhead of multi-instance clustering. The absence of bundled local storage and GPUs makes it a highly specialized, compute-and-memory-focused resource. It is ideally suited for large-scale database operations, in-memory data grids like Redis, software compilation, and CPU-based LLM inference tasks.
